1.1.text:
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 43
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle victims of violence against Women and Children obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 10
(1) The community is obligated and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the authorized parties; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
(2) The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 58
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
e. enhancement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of DPPKBPP-PA.

Article 51
(1) The repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.
(2) The repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement the repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 49
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions of law enforcement officials provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.

b. security officers; and

General

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 36
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.

CHILD PARTICIPATION
Article 55
(1) Every Child has the right to participate in conveying opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.

Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 36
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.
(2) The care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social sector.
(3) In the event that a Child is neglected due to any reason where the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or the Regency Government or Community Organizations as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
(4) The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) shall simultaneously determine the shelter and care facility for the neglected Child concerned.

Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) occurs.

Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 51
(1) The repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.
(2) The repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement the repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 14
(1) Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of Women's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may give rise to violations of Women's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of unregistered marriages/siri marriages.
(2) Efforts made in order to prevent violations of Children's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of marriage at child age.

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 36
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.
(2) The care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social sector.

a. directly;

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 14
(1) Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of Women's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may give rise to violations of Women's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of unregistered marriages/siri marriages.
(2) Efforts made in order to prevent violations of Children's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of marriage at child age.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 58
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
e. enhancement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of DPPKBPP-PA.

Article 37
(1) The Regency Government shall organize skills training for street children and neglected children.

(1) The Regency Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:

Article 36
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.
(2) The care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social sector.
(3) In the event that a Child is neglected due to any reason where the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or the Regency Government or Community Organizations as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
(4) The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) shall simultaneously determine the shelter and care facility for the neglected Child concerned.

29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which is formed by the government or community-based. 34. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) occurs.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.

b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out mentoring/social guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

Article 47
(1) The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a Safe House include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of Safe House services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of Safe House services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 51
(1) The repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.
(2) The repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement the repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
